risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: internal GMM lags only, no controls, causal wording ('causal-effect relationship'), lag order unreported.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: PCA index of fixed, mobile and internet, arbitrary units, interpolation used.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: region-based sample of 73 incl. high-income economies, interpolation, 2000-2018.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: RGDP level (apparently logged, Table 4 mean 23.899 vs 'billion dollars' in Table 1) used as growth proxy; HDI composite.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: serious; lag order not reported, I(1) series with cointegration and no ECM, unit-root tables erratic.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: serious; abstract, text and conclusion claim positive ICT effects on growth in all regions while Table 11 prints negative coefficients (entire, SSA, LAAC), and p-values/stars are inconsistent with Table 10.
risk_of_bias.why: Serious overall is appropriate: causal framing without exogenous variation, no controls, and abstract/text contradict the printed table.

problems: Extractor's table reading is right: Table 11 signs are negative for ICT(t-1) in the RGDP equation (entire -0.437, SSA -0.548, LAAC -0.406) and positive only for MENA (0.435). Abstract, p.14727 text ('growth will increase by 0.01%') and conclusion ('positive and significant impact on growth') contradict the table; the authors also misread -0.437/-0.548/-0.406 as growth-to-ICT effects (p.14728), while their own policy section says 'negative impact of ICT on economic growth at the panel level' (p.14737) and 'significant negative impact of technology (ICT)' (p.14738).
